## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The `users.legacy_email` drop must take a backup before merge, because the migration removes the column without the `backup_table` call that `migrations/safety.py` requires of every destructive migration. The `orders.coupon_code` drop takes its backup, and the added test asserts it.

## Changes
The pull request adds migrations 3 and 4, which drop `users.legacy_email` and `orders.coupon_code`. It also adds one test that runs all four migrations and checks that both columns are gone and that `orders_backup_4` holds the coupon code.

## Critical
- migrations/m0003_drop_legacy_email.py:7 — correctness — Call backup_table before dropping users.legacy_email — Any `users` row with a `legacy_email` value loses it when migration 3 runs, because `upgrade` creates no `users_backup_3`. `migrations/safety.py:3-5` says each destructive migration first calls `backup_table`; only the older `users_backup_2` snapshot still holds the column. — `legacy_email` values written after migration 2 ran cannot be recovered once this deploys, and rolling back the deploy does not restore them. — Fix: Add `backup_table(conn, "users", VERSION)` as in `migrations/m0004_drop_coupon_code.py:7`, and extend `test_drop_retired_columns` with a `users` row and a `users_backup_3` assertion.
